what_its_for: Paricalcitol is used to prevent and treat a condition called secondary hyperparathyroidism, which means your parathyroid glands are making too much parathyroid hormone (PTH). This happens in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) whose kidneys are not working well enough to keep the right balance of calcium and phosphorus in the body. Keeping PTH levels under control helps protect your bones and heart.
how_to_take: Paricalcitol comes as a capsule you swallow by mouth OR as an injection given into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider, usually during dialysis. Take the capsule with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. If you receive the injection form, it will be given to you at your dialysis center by a nurse or doctor. Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribes.
dosing: Your doctor will choose your dose based on your PTH levels, calcium levels, phosphorus levels, and how well your kidneys are working. The dose is different for every person and may be adjusted over time. Common starting doses for capsules range from 1 mcg to 2 mcg taken daily or 3 times per week. Do not change your dose on your own. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to find the right dose for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the capsule, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss a dose at your dialysis session, contact your dialysis center or doctor for guidance.
storage: Store paricalcitol capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original packaging. Protect them from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist how to do this.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking extra vitamin D supplements or calcium supplements unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not use antacids that contain magnesium while taking paricalcitol unless your doctor approves, as this can raise magnesium levels too high. Limit foods that are very high in phosphorus (such as dairy, cola drinks, processed foods, and nuts) unless your doctor or dietitian says otherwise. Avoid getting dehydrated, as this can affect your calcium and kidney function.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of these warning signs, which may mean your calcium levels are too high (hypercalcemia): nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite, feeling very tired or weak, confusion or difficulty thinking clearly, increased thirst or urination, muscle or bone pain, or irregular heartbeat. Also call your doctor if you notice swelling, unusual weight gain, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Paricalcitol starts working to lower your PTH levels within a few weeks, but it may take several weeks to months before your doctor sees the full benefit through your blood test results. You may not feel any different right away — that is normal. Your doctor will check your blood regularly to make sure the medicine is working and that your calcium and phosphorus levels stay in a safe range. It is important to keep all your lab appointments.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using paricalcitol, as it may not be safe for your baby. Children can use paricalcitol but the dose will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on weight and age. Older adults should be monitored closely because they may be more sensitive to changes in calcium levels. People with liver disease should let their doctor know, as this can affect how the body processes the medication.
